Subject: Re: [Escalation] Acme AI p99 regressions — need status page + mitigation

Thanks for the escalation. Quick summary from SRE (Connor) and infra:
- Root cause (prelim): routing policy mismatch after yesterday's model-variant rollout caused a small subset of requests to be routed to a non-quantized variant on G4 pools leading to tail latency under burst load.
- Impacted: <5% of requests for certain seq-length distributions -> large p99 skew.
- Mitigation applied: temporarily pinned routing to the stable quantized variant and increased pool capacity in us-west-2. We also enabled a temporary prefix-KV cache bypass for affected endpoints.
- Visible improvement: p99 reduced from ~11s to ~1.2s within ~18 minutes of the mitigation. Error rates also fell back to baseline.

Action items (post-incident):
1) Postmortem doc with timeline and rollout guardrails (Assigned: Connor).
2) Add a routing policy test to our rollout CI so future rollouts run a small latency-focused canary for tail latency (Assigned: Infra Eng).
3) Customer comms: Monica to send an update with root cause, mitigation and next steps. Rishi to offer a short-term credit or capacity bump if Acme requests.

Connor — please paste the small status page blurb and confirm the updated metrics so Monica can push the customer update.

-Markus
Markus Klein
VP Engineering, Redwood Inference

Hi Alex — thanks again for flagging and for the sample logs. Quick update and next steps:

What happened (TL;DR): a recent model-variant rollout caused a small percentage of requests to be routed to a non-quantized variant on the G4 pool, which under burst traffic produced long tail latency (p99).

What we did:
- Immediately pinned routing to the stable quantized variant and increased pool capacity in us-west-2.
- Enabled a temporary cache bypass reduction for affected endpoints.
- Observed p99 improve from ~11s down to ~1.2s in ~18 minutes. Error rates returned to baseline.

What's next (follow-up items):
- Connor will publish a postmortem with timeline and root cause analysis (expected Thursday, 2026-12-09).
- We'll add a latency-focused canary to rollout CI and tighten routing policy checks (engineering ticket created: RDW-OPS-1376).
- Rishi will follow up on any commercial remediation (credits/capacity) if needed.

We've posted a short incident note on our status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-12-05-p99-regression
We also attached a snapshot of our internal metrics for the window you sent earlier.

If you'd like immediate capacity while we complete the follow-up work, Rishi and I can provision a short-term reserved pool for you. Let us know.

Apologies again for the disruption — we appreciate your patience and the quick reporting which helped us remediate faster.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior AM, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
